In [[mathematics]], specifically [[algebraic geometry]], the '''valuative criteria''' are a collection of results that make it possible to decide whether a [[morphism]] of [[algebraic variety|algebraic varieties]], or more generally [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]]s, is [[universally closed]], [[Glossary of algebraic geometry#separated|separated]], or [[proper morphism|proper]].

== Statement of the valuative criteria ==
Recall that a [[valuation ring]] ''A'' is a domain, so if ''K'' is the [[field of fractions]] of ''A'', then Spec ''K'' is the [[generic point]] of Spec ''A''.

Let ''X'' and ''Y'' be schemes, and let ''f'' : ''X'' &rarr; ''Y'' be a morphism of schemes. Then the following are equivalent:<ref>EGA II, proposition 7.2.3 and théorème 7.3.8.</ref><ref>Stacks Project, tags 01KA, 01KY, and 0BX4.</ref>
#''f'' is separated (resp. universally closed, resp. proper)
#''f'' is [[quasi-separated]] (resp. [[quasi-compact morphism|quasi-compact]], resp. of finite type and quasi-separated) and for every valuation ring ''A'', if ''Y' '' = Spec ''A'' and ''X' '' denotes the generic point of ''Y' '', then for every morphism ''Y' '' &rarr; ''Y'' and every morphism ''X' '' &rarr; ''X'' which lifts the generic point, then there exists at most one (resp. at least one, resp. exactly one) lift ''Y' '' &rarr; ''X''.

The lifting condition is equivalent to specifying that the natural morphism
:<math>\text{Hom}_Y(Y', X) \to \text{Hom}_Y(\operatorname{Spec} K, X)</math>
is injective (resp. surjective, resp. bijective).

Furthermore, in the special case when ''Y'' is (locally) [[Noetherian scheme|Noetherian]], it suffices to check the case that ''A'' is a [[discrete valuation ring]].
